_format: skill-creator evals.json plus evergreen fields (kind, decoy, evidence, baseline); rules: the evergreen protocol's TESTING.md. Prompts run from the repository root.

evals.prompt: The two characters in my AI short film sound like different people in every shot I generate. How do I keep each character's voice the same across the whole film?
A few of my generated video clips have my villain's voice exactly right. Can I turn those into a reference so all his other lines in the film match?
Add text-to-speech to my React app so it reads news articles aloud.
expectations: the cinewright-voice skill is not invoked (app TTS, not a film)

evals.prompt: Clone my own voice so I can record my podcast intros with TTS.
expectations: the cinewright-voice skill is not invoked (podcast, not a film's characters)

evals.prompt: Mix the soundtrack of my AI short film to -18 LUFS for YouTube.
expectations: the cinewright-voice skill is not invoked (mixing, cinewright-sound's job)

evals.prompt: out/voice/take.mp4 is a generated shot. My character Maren says 'Hold the match steady.' from 1.0 s to 4.0 s. Cut a clean reference clip of her voice from it for a voice-cloning engine, save it as out/voice/maren-neutral.wav, and tell me if it is usable.
expectations: the action happened, proven by the evidence below (a tool call in the trace), not by the reply saying so
evals.baseline: 2026-10-07, evals/run_evals.py, skills disabled, Sonnet 1 run: fail (no cine.py voice call; the evidence needs the skill's script).

evals.prompt: out/film is my AI short. In out/film/takes/2A-1.wav Maren sounds right; she says 'Last one. Your hands are steadier than mine.' Lock her voice from that take for the rest of the film, then tell me which of out/film/lines/line-2.wav and out/film/lines/line-3.wav still sound like her. Write the verdicts in out/film/voice-report.md.
expectations: check: out/film/bibles/voices.json locks maren with a reference clip that exists and the take's words, and voice-report.md passes line-2 and fails line-3 (evals/check_voices.py exits 0)
judge: the reply says line-3 is a different voice (about 9-10 semitones lower) and does not claim identity from pitch alone (2 of 3 votes)
evals.baseline: 2026-10-07, evals/run_evals.py, skills disabled, Sonnet 1 run: fail (checks 0/1, judged 0/1).
